LoloBuy fees explained: what you pay and when

A useful budget separates the first product payment from the later parcel payment. This guide shows where domestic freight, payment handling, currency conversion, optional services, international shipping and final adjustments fit.

Editorial note: This independent guide is based on LoloBuy’s public purchase, payment, domestic-delivery, shipping-deposit and weight-adjustment materials, checked on 4 October 2026. Rates and available methods can change by transaction, currency, route and destination; always use the amount shown in the live checkout.

Why there is no single LoloBuy checkout total

The clearest way to have LoloBuy fees explained is to stop treating an agent order like a normal one-payment store purchase. LoloBuy’s public workflow separates buying an item in China from sending a finished parcel overseas. The first payment gets the selected product into the warehouse. The later payment covers the international parcel after its contents and shipping route are known.

That separation matters because several amounts are unknown at the beginning. The seller may charge Chinese domestic delivery. The warehouse may record a weight different from the seller’s estimate. Your packed parcel can occupy more space than its scale weight suggests. The chosen payment channel may add handling, and a route may calculate customs-related amounts from declared value. A sensible budget is therefore a ledger, not one screenshot.

This article does not publish a universal percentage, exchange rate or shipping price. Those numbers can change and may not apply to your account. Instead, it explains which line items to identify, when they appear and which ones can still be adjusted.

Stage one: product price and Chinese domestic delivery

The first LoloBuy order cost starts with the seller’s product price for the exact option and quantity you selected. Save the listing, variant, quantity and order total before paying. If a seller changes a price after the order is submitted, LoloBuy’s help material says an outstanding balance can appear. Do not approve that difference blindly: compare it with the saved listing and make sure the agent is purchasing the intended version.

Chinese domestic delivery is the seller-to-warehouse journey. It is separate from international shipping. A listing may include domestic delivery, charge it per order or require an adjustment after the seller confirms the package. LoloBuy states that items from the same seller checked out together may incur the domestic delivery charge once, although extra quantity or weight can still create an additional amount.

That makes grouping a potential efficiency, not a guaranteed discount. Confirm that the seller identity is actually the same and that the items can be ordered together. Never add unwanted products merely to chase a delivery saving. Record domestic freight as its own line so it is not later mistaken for international postage.

Stage two: payment-channel fee and currency conversion

A LoloBuy payment fee can be added by the selected channel. The public checkout wording describes its handling charge as a rate applied to the actual payment plus any fixed component shown for that method. The important word is shown: use the live transaction summary, because the fee can differ by payment method and can change without making an old guide technically false.

If you pay in a currency other than Chinese yuan, conversion is another part of the real cost. LoloBuy’s interface says foreign currency is converted to CNY using the platform exchange rate. It also explains that this can differ from a headline market rate because exchange rates move and banks may impose cross-border remittance costs. Your card issuer or bank may separately apply its own conversion or international-transaction terms.

Before confirming payment, write down four numbers: the CNY order amount, the currency you will actually pay, the platform conversion shown and the final amount charged by the channel. The difference between the first and last number is not automatically one mysterious “agent fee.” It can combine channel handling and conversion effects.

Choose from the methods visible on your transaction

LoloBuy’s current public purchase guide lists credit cards, WeChat, Alipay, Chinese debit cards and bank telegraphic transfer. That list describes the public workflow, not a promise that every method is available for every buyer, country, currency or payment size. The payment screen on your own order is the operational source.

Compare methods on total charged, not on the fee label alone. A method with a lower visible handling percentage may produce a different currency result or bank charge. Also check the billing details and refund destination before paying. A low-friction method is not necessarily the lowest final cost if your bank converts the transaction again.

Standard purchasing work versus optional services

LoloBuy’s current public help page describes its standard purchasing service as having a zero service fee. Standard warehouse inspection is also described as free. These statements do not mean that every action surrounding an order costs zero, nor do they eliminate product, domestic delivery, payment-channel or international shipping charges.

Optional value-added services can be selected during the workflow. Depending on what is currently offered, a buyer may see choices related to additional photos, measurements, detailed inspection, packaging or parcel treatment. Only add a service when it answers a specific question or reduces a concrete shipping risk. Read its live description and price before authorizing it; availability and scope can change.

Free standard inspection also has boundaries. It covers visible checks such as style, quantity, colour, size, model and obvious appearance issues. It is not a universal authenticity, performance or electronics test. Paying for a separate service should likewise not be interpreted as a guarantee beyond the service description.

Stage three: the international shipping deposit

After items are stored and you submit a parcel, LoloBuy calculates an international shipping deposit. The public workflow says this estimate uses factors including estimated weight, route and destination. This is the second major payment stage, not a duplicate of the domestic delivery already paid to move products into the warehouse.

The cheapest displayed route is not automatically the cheapest valid route. Compare whether the line accepts the product category, which weight it bills, its packaging restrictions, tracking coverage, customs model and delivery estimate. A route can use actual scale weight or a volumetric calculation based on parcel dimensions. Bulky packaging can therefore matter even when the products are light.

Before paying, save the parcel contents, destination, route name, estimated weight, parcel dimensions if shown, declared value, shipping deposit and any tax-related line. This creates a reliable baseline for understanding a later refund or supplemental payment.

Why the final shipping amount may change

The initial parcel figure is an estimate. LoloBuy’s public instructions say the carrier verifies the final package size and weight. If the actual logistics cost is lower than the deposit, the difference can be returned to the buyer’s LoloBuy account. If it is higher, a supplemental payment may be required.

A difference is not automatically an error. It can result from the final carton, protective material, packaging removal, measurement, route billing rules or a mismatch between estimated and actual product weight. Compare the final weight and dimensions with the saved estimate before deciding whether to question it.

If the adjustment is unclear, ask for the estimated weight, final scale weight, final dimensions, chargeable weight and the route’s calculation rule. A question such as “Why did shipping change?” is harder to investigate than “The deposit used 3.2 kg; the final record shows 4.1 kg chargeable weight—was the difference actual or volumetric?”

Tax, customs and declared value are separate decisions

International shipping does not erase destination-country import rules. Some routes can display tax or customs-related amounts based on the declared value, and LoloBuy’s public help notes that a declared USD value may be converted into RMB using a current exchange rate for the calculation. The exact treatment depends on the route and destination.

Do not assume that “tax-free,” prepaid tax, declared-value handling or customs clearance means the same thing across every line. Read the current route details and use a truthful declaration. A calculator or another buyer’s old parcel cannot guarantee how customs will assess yours. This guide deliberately avoids country-specific thresholds because they can change and require official destination-country verification.

Build a seven-line cost ledger

A simple ledger keeps estimates and settled costs from being mixed together. Use these seven lines:

  1. Products: final seller price for the selected options and quantities.
  2. Domestic delivery: seller-to-warehouse freight and any later seller adjustment.
  3. Payment: channel handling, fixed component and currency conversion visible at checkout.
  4. Optional services: only services you explicitly selected.
  5. International deposit: the estimated parcel shipping amount before carrier verification.
  6. Tax or customs-related amount: only what the chosen route currently displays.
  7. Final adjustment: balance refund or supplemental payment after final measurement.

Give each line three columns: estimated, paid and settled. The total “paid” column tells you cash outlay so far; the “settled” column is the useful final record. Keep a refund to account balance separate from a refund to your original payment method. They are not the same event, even when the amounts match.

Checks to make before each payment

Before the product payment: confirm the option, quantity, seller price, domestic freight, payment currency, channel handling and displayed final charge. Save the order summary.

Before the parcel payment: confirm every included item, route eligibility, estimated and chargeable weight logic, packaging choices, declaration, destination and international shipping deposit. Do not submit while an unresolved QC or return question remains.

After dispatch: record final weight and dimensions, the settled international charge, any account-balance return and any supplemental payment. If an amount changes, identify the line that changed before opening a support request.

Conclusion: budget by stage, not by headline rate

The practical answer to “What are the LoloBuy fees?” is a timeline. First come the product, Chinese domestic delivery and payment effects. Optional services appear only when selected. Later, the international shipping deposit, route-specific tax treatment and final carrier adjustment complete the parcel cost.

Separating these stages makes comparison more honest and support questions more precise. It also prevents a free standard service from being confused with a free order, or a shipping deposit from being mistaken for the settled charge. Use the live checkout for every rate and keep a small ledger until the parcel’s final amount is recorded.
